claims.text: At least 15 people were killed in a Russian double-tap drone strike on a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih.
130 people, including 23 children, were injured in the drone attack on Kryvyi Rih's largest mall.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the second wave of the drone strike targeted emergency workers responding to the scene.
Separate Russian attacks in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region killed four people, including three children.
Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, with Moscow currently controlling about a fifth of Ukrainian territory.
A Russian drone strike on a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih killed 14 people and injured over 100, including 22 children.
Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Ganzha stated that drone strikes on a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre killed 14 people and wounded 121 others.
The Coalition of the Willing meeting on Ukraine's independence day will be co-chaired by French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
A Ukrainian drone attack killed one person and wounded four others when it struck a car in Russia's Belgorod region near Razumnoye.
Volodymyr Zelensky stated that a Ukrainian drone attack hit an oil refinery in Perm and the Marinovka military airfield in Volgograd.
A separate Russian drone strike in the Kharkiv region killed two women, aged 73 and 66, and injured two others.
Russia's Defence Ministry stated its air defences intercepted 325 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions and Crimea.

Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced that Turkey requested Interpol red notices for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and another suspect over the May attack on the Global Sumud Flotilla.
Arrest warrants were issued by Turkey on July 14 against 35 people on charges including genocide, crimes against humanity, and torture related to the Gaza aid flotilla interception.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office called Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan antisemitic and stated his attempt to intimidate Israeli leaders will go nowhere.
Turkish arrest warrants were issued for Israeli soldier Afek Moskovitch on charges including genocide and torture.
France, Italy, and Australia have launched judicial proceedings regarding Israel's detention of activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla.
Benjamin Netanyahu's office called Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an antisemitic dictator who massacred Kurds and supports Hamas.
Syria accused Israel of striking a disused military air base near Aleppo.
Three judges in Hong Kong convicted former Tiananmen vigil organisers Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung for incitement to subversion.
Activists Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison under Hong Kong's national security law.
Former Hong Kong lawmaker Albert Ho, a co-defendant in the subversion trial, pleaded guilty in January.
Chow Hang-tung wrote a letter from prison to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham urging Britain to adopt a more robust stance against China.
The subversion case against the Hong Kong Alliance centred on its slogan demanding an end to one-party rule.
The Hong Kong Alliance was founded in May 1989 to support student pro-democracy rallies in Beijing.
Hong Kong's top court overturned Chow Hang-tung's conviction in 2022 regarding her 2021 arrest for inciting the public to join the Tiananmen vigil.
Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was returned to Adiala Jail hours after being taken to an Islamabad hospital for a court-ordered medical examination.
Relatives of Imran Khan stated that he is being subjected to torture in prison.
Imran Khan's son Kasim stated in February that Khan lost most of the vision in his right eye, with only 15% eyesight remaining.
Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi were sentenced in January 2025 to 14 years and seven years in prison, respectively, in a corruption case.
Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar stated that a team of qualified doctors declared Imran Khan medically fit following his hospital examination.
Imran Khan was transferred to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences instead of the court-ordered private Shifa International Hospital due to security concerns.
A senior police official told the BBC that the heavy police presence outside Shifa International Hospital was used as a decoy.
Imran Khan was initially arrested in 2023, sentenced to three years in prison on corruption charges, and disqualified from politics for five years.
The UK, Australia, and Canada issued a joint statement calling Israel's decision not to conduct a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strike on a World Central Kitchen convoy shameful.
Seven World Central Kitchen aid workers, including three Britons, an Australian, a Pole, a dual US-Canadian national, and a Palestinian, were killed in an Israeli drone strike in April 2024.
Poland and Australia summoned Israel's ambassadors after the Israeli military announced it would not pursue criminal investigations into the World Central Kitchen convoy attack.
A joint statement by the UK, Australia, and Canada noted that 186 humanitarian workers were killed in Gaza in 2025.

The Israeli military announced it will conduct a criminal investigation into the killing of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab and six relatives, as well as the March 2025 killing of 15 Palestinians.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband described Israel's tender for 1,200 settlement homes in the West Bank's E1 area as an unacceptable and destructive act.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar rejected Ed Miliband's statement, asserting that the Jewish people have the right to live throughout the Land of Israel.
One of the Israeli military officers dismissed over the World Central Kitchen strike had previously signed an open letter calling for Gaza to be deprived of humanitarian aid.
US President Donald Trump threatened a 50 percent tariff on approximately $20 billion worth of Canadian goods starting Saturday at 12:01am EDT.
Canadian Minister Dominic LeBlanc met US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer for over three hours in Washington, DC to negotiate a trade deal.
A Leger Opinion poll showed that 56 percent of Canadians do not want Prime Minister Mark Carney to make further trade concessions to the US.
In a leaked audio recording, US Vice President JD Vance mocked Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney for attempting to out-tough Donald Trump.
Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew called Donald Trump very weak and urged Canada to fight rather than make concessions.
The White House stated that Canadian imports of US alcohol dropped approximately 81 percent year-on-year following Canadian retaliatory measures.
Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston and Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew confirmed that Prime Minister Mark Carney asked Canadian provinces to allow US alcohol back on store shelves.
Rahul Gandhi staged a seven-hour sit-in outside the office of New Delhi's Deputy Commissioner of Police demanding an FIR over pellet gun injuries to 19-year-old student Sahil Lochab.
Sahil Lochab sustained over 200 pellets in his body and lost vision in his right eye during the July 20 student march in Delhi.
Delhi Police registered an FIR under Sections 118(1) and 125 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita following Rahul Gandhi's sit-in protest.
The Supreme Court constituted a five-member High-Powered Enquiry Committee headed by a former Supreme Court judge to investigate police action during the July 20 protest.
A general diary entry at the Sansad Marg police station recorded two rounds fired from anti-riot guns by RAF personnel, while a CRPF inquiry found RAF personnel fired seven pellet rounds.
Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25 following opposition protests over police action against student demonstrators.
Union Minister JP Nadda criticized Rahul Gandhi's sit-in as camera-centric drama designed to distract from criticism regarding the national song and flag.
Rahul Gandhi claimed that final approval to register the FIR came directly from Home Secretary and Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju claimed that no protester was seriously injured or suffered broken bones during the July 20 police action.
The Indian government estimated sugar production for the current season at 306 lakh tonnes, 11 percent lower than the initial estimate of 343 lakh tonnes.
The Indian government permitted the duty-free import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar to stabilize domestic prices.
Retail sugar prices in India reached Rs 58.2 per kg, representing a 20 percent increase over the previous month.
The share of Indian sugar diverted for ethanol production declined from around 12 percent in 2022-23 to around 9 percent in 2025-26.
Odisha registered the highest retail sugar price in India at Rs 64.72 per kg, up Rs 17.80 compared to the same date in 2025.
The Indian government imposed a stock limit of 400 tonnes on sugar dealers from August 1 to November 30.
International sugar prices rose more than 16 percent to $552 per tonne on August 20, up from $474 per tonne on June 30.
As of August 20, 97 percent of sugarcane dues for the 2025-26 season had been paid to Indian farmers.
External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed that 22 Indian seafarers aboard two hijacked merchant vessels off Yemen and Somalia are safe.
The Eritrea-flagged oil products tanker MT Sibu 1, carrying 16 Indians among 20 crew members, was hijacked by six armed pirates off the coast of Yemen on August 20.
The Cameroon-flagged cargo ship MV Lutuf, carrying six Indians among 10 crew members, was hijacked off Somalia's Puntland coast on August 17.
The MV Lutuf was carrying Turkish weapons, communications, and satellite equipment bound for a Turkish military training facility in Mogadishu.
Eight armed pirates carrying AK-47-type weapons boarded the MV Lutuf from two skiffs and forced the crew from the citadel to the bridge.
The 2026 BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report estimates India supplies 311,936 seafarers, making it the second-largest supplier globally.
The Supreme Court of India ruled in a 2-1 majority that advocates with one year of practice are eligible to apply for entry-level judicial officer posts, reducing the prior three-year requirement.
Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice A G Masih formed the majority opinion, while Justice Vinod Chandran dissented.
Selected judicial candidates will undergo a mandatory two-year post-selection training period, receiving fixed emoluments equal to half the salary of magistrates during their first year.
Candidates applying for Civil Judge recruitment between May 25, 2025, and March 31, 2027, will be deemed to meet the one-year legal practice requirement without needing to provide proof certificates.
Starting April 1, 2027, candidates applying for Civil Judge recruitment must produce a certificate of proof of practice showing participation in effective judicial proceedings.
The post-selection judicial training program includes one year at a State judicial academy, six months of clerkship under a Principal District Judge, and six months under a High Court judge.
